title: Boss: one researcher, three browser bugs
summary: A bug bounty report chains a stored XSS on the staff dashboard, a CSRF on the email change and a hand-written CORS handler that trusts every origin. Fix all three so the chain breaks at every link.

steps.title: Report #5120: account takeover of shop staff
body: 1. Stored XSS. My display name is and it runs
on /staff/users for every member of staff. My website field  javascript:alert(1)  is
written into an href as well.
2. CSRF. /profile/email accepts GET, so a link changes a victim's email:
POSTs from other sites work too.
3. CORS. The API copies any Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials:
Chained: the XSS or any page on `evil.example` reads a victim's orders through CORS and changes their email through CSRF. Fix each link.

steps.title: Link 1: the staff dashboard
prompt: - the name is HTML-encoded **everywhere** it appears (the `data-name` attribute and the link text);
- the website is used as the `href` only when it is an absolute `http` or `https` URL (`Uri.TryCreate(..., UriKind.Absolute, ...)` and the scheme); otherwise the `href` is `#`. Encode it as well.
starter: var users = new List<(string Name, string Website)>
solution: var users = new List<(string Name, string Website)>
Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out var u) && (u.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttps || u.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttp) ? url : "#";
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("The dashboard could be loaded", async () =>
var p = await DojoWeb.Text(await http.GetAsync("/staff/users"));
var enc = System.Text.Encodings.Web.HtmlEncoder.Default;
Dojo.Check("the name is not a tag", !p.Contains("
Dojo.Check("...it is shown as text", p.Contains(">" + enc.Encode("") + ""), p);
Dojo.Check("a quote in a name cannot break out of data-name", !p.Contains("data-name=\"Quote \" Person\"") && p.Contains("data-name=\"" + enc.Encode("Quote \" Person") + "\""), p);
Dojo.Check("no javascript: link", !p.Contains("javascript:"), p);
Dojo.Check("Mallory's link is #", p.Contains("Mallory"), p);
Dojo.Check("Ada's https link still works", p.Contains("Ada"), p);
Dojo.Check("an http link keeps its query, encoded for HTML", p.Contains("href=\"" + enc.Encode("http://quote.example/?a=1&b=2") + "\""), p);
hints: `var enc = HtmlEncoder.Default;` and `enc.Encode(u.Name)` in both places.
A helper: `string SafeHref(string url) => Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out var u) && (u.Scheme == "https" || u.Scheme == "http") ? url : "#";`, then `enc.Encode(SafeHref(u.Website))`.

steps.title: Link 2: the email change
prompt: - it accepts **POST only** (a GET must not change anything);

- a middleware refuses unsafe methods (anything but GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) with `403` unless `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `same-origin` or `none`; when the header is missing, allow it only if `Origin` is missing or exactly `https://shop.example`.
starter: // The old mobile app still uses GET.
solution: var allowed = site.Length > 0 ? site is "same-origin" or "none" : origin.Length == 0 || origin == "https://shop.example";
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Post(HttpClient http, string to, string? site, string? origin)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/profile/email") { Content = new FormUrlEncodedContent(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["email"] = to }) };
if (site is not null) msg.Headers.Add("Sec-Fetch-Site", site);
if (origin is not null) msg.Headers.Add("Origin", origin);
return http.SendAsync(msg);
static async Task<string?> Email(HttpClient http) => DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/profile")), "email");
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("The email change could be checked", async () =>
var g = await http.GetAsync("/profile/email?email=me@evil.example");
Dojo.Check("GET /profile/email?email=... is refused", (int)g.StatusCode >= 400, ((int)g.StatusCode).ToString());
DojoWeb.Status("a cross-site POST is refused", 403, await Post(http, "me@evil.example", "cross-site", "https://evil.example"));
DojoWeb.Status("a POST with a foreign Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site is refused", 403, await Post(http, "me@evil.example", null, "https://evil.example"));
Dojo.Eq("the email is unchanged", "ada@customer.example", await Email(http));
DojoWeb.Status("the shop's own form works", 200, await Post(http, "ada.new@customer.example", "same-origin", "https://shop.example"));
Dojo.Eq("...and changes the email", "ada.new@customer.example", await Email(http));
hints: `app.MapPost("/profile/email", ...)` reading only the form. A GET to it then gets 405 automatically.
The Fetch Metadata middleware from the CSRF lesson goes before the endpoints.

steps.title: Link 3: the hand-written CORS handler
prompt: Someone wrote CORS by hand. Keep it hand-written, but make it safe:

- only the origins `https://app.shop.example` and `https://admin.shop.example` get `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (their own value) and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`; every other origin, `null` included, gets **no** CORS headers;
- every response that depends on `Origin` says so with `Vary: Origin` (so a cache never serves one origin's answer to another);
- pages cannot be framed: `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` on every response.
solution: if (allowed.Contains(origin))   // exact match: no prefixes, no suffixes, no "null"
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
static async Task<HttpResponseMessage> Get(HttpClient http, string? origin)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "/api/orders");
if (origin is not null) msg.Headers.Add("Origin", origin);
return await http.SendAsync(msg);
static string? H(HttpResponseMessage r, string name) => r.Headers.TryGetValues(name, out var v) ? string.Join(",", v) : null;
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("CORS could be checked", async () =>
var app1 = await Get(http, "https://app.shop.example");
Dojo.Eq("the SPA gets its own origin back", "https://app.shop.example", H(app1, "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"));
Dojo.Eq("...with credentials", "true", H(app1, "Access-Control-Allow-Credentials"));
Dojo.Eq("the admin app is allowed too", "https://admin.shop.example", H(await Get(http, "https://admin.shop.example"), "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"));
foreach (var o in new[] { "https://evil.example", "null", "https://app.shop.example.evil.example", "https://evilapp.shop.example", "http://app.shop.example" })
var r = await Get(http, o);
Dojo.Eq($"{o} gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin", null, H(r, "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"));
Dojo.Eq($"{o} gets no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials", null, H(r, "Access-Control-Allow-Credentials"));
Dojo.Check("Vary: Origin is set", (app1.Headers.Vary.Contains("Origin")), string.Join(",", app1.Headers.Vary));
var none = await Get(http, null);
Dojo.Check("frame-ancestors 'none' on every response", (H(none, "Content-Security-Policy") ?? "").Contains("frame-ancestors 'none'"), H(none, "Content-Security-Policy") ?? "(none)");
hints: An exact `HashSet<string>` of allowed origins, and `if (allowed.Contains(origin)) { ... }` around the two CORS headers.
